correctness.rationale: Fort rigidity from r_v>=2 proves an exhaustive minimal-fort classification; the stalled-white-set characterization of standard zero forcing proves a fort-hitting criterion. A three-case independent local partition indexed by zero forcing sets of G gives exact coefficients. All hypothesis boundaries checked, including isolated and disconnected base vertices. Direct simulation verified 104 corona instances and 537504 subsets. Computations corroborate rather than certify the general proof.

originality.rationale: Primary 2024 full-text Proposition 22 gives only one local class and Proposition 23 a cycle-base lift, warning general-graph failure for r=1. The present exact r_v>=2 all-base converse and entire ZF polynomial are not implied by them. The previously known 2016 scalar minimum is disclaimed as prior-implied; 2018 polynomial framework lacks this corona transfer. Eight targeted published-finding corpus searches and directly relevant own-claim comparisons did not identify an equivalent statement. Publication priority remains provisional due to later/inaccessible sources.

value.rationale: The complete transformation describes every size coefficient for clique coronas of every finite simple base and arbitrary varying clique sizes. A simultaneous exact minimal-fort-hypergraph classification and minimum-set multiplicities strictly refine the previously known scalar forcing number, and the essential size-two peripheral threshold explains why a natural stronger generalization fails at size one.
